image_description: A bassoon standing vertically against a wall in a dimly lit room. The instrument features a dark reddish-brown wooden body with complex silver metal keywork. A curved metal bocal is attached to the top joint, and the bell section points upward. The background includes a white textured wall on the left and dark shadows/cardboard boxes on the right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument spans nearly the full height of the frame, consistent with the ~1.3m length of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The boot joint at the bottom connects the two main parallel tubes, creating the characteristic U-profile, and the bell flares upward at the top right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior; only the external tube arrangement can be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct curved metal tube (bocal) protrudes from the upper wing joint, ready for a reed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Complex silver keywork with rods and pads is clearly visible running along the length of the wooden body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell section at the top right shows the correct outward flare. While not being played, the diagonal orientation of the bell relative to the boot joint is accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits the correct deep reddish-brown hue typical of maple or rosewood bassoons, with some specular highlights indicating a polished finish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keywork reflects light with a silver/chrome appearance, consistent with standard nickel-silver or silver-plated keys.
The main body segments are clearly constructed from turned wood.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white wall has a slightly repetitive, noisy texture pattern that lacks natural variation, suggestive of AI generation noise rather than real plaster/paint texture.

artifact_observations.location: Keywork near the boot joint (bottom center)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The mechanical linkage of the keys near the U-bend appears somewhat fused and indistinct. Individual rods and pads merge into each other slightly, lacking the crisp separation expected in high-fidelity macro photography of complex machinery.
The flare of the bell seems slightly asymmetrical and the rim thickness varies inconsistently, though this could be partly due to the low lighting angle.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument and rule out look-alikes like contrabassoon or fake woodwind props.
To verify the structural integrity of the complex metal keys and ensure they are distinct physical objects attached to the wood, not melted artifacts.
To assess the realism of the lighting, shadows, and wood grain texture, and detect subtle generative noise.
To ensure the instrument is properly grounded in 3D space and not bleeding into the background wall.

focus_areas: Integrity of metal keywork mechanisms (fusion/melting checks)
Wood grain texture realism and continuity
Geometric accuracy of the U-shaped boot joint
Lighting consistency on reflective metal surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the connectivity of the metal keys. AI often struggles with the intricate rod-and-pad systems of woodwinds, resulting in 'mushy' or fused mechanics. Verify if the wood grain follows the cylindrical form of the instrument correctly or if it smears. Check the bocal connection point for any geometric impossibilities.
